course: Risk Theory, M.Sc. Actuarial Sciences, Shahid Beheshti University, Spring 1405

contributors.adaptations: The submitted 1,000-row motor aggregate supplied the original calibration target. The current portfolio page uses the approved deterministic entity-first v2 replacement: 10,000 vehicles, separate coverage-specific policies, physical accidents, compatible claim files and components, and exactly reconciled insurer-paid losses over 1,000 synthetic months. It presents selected-month metrics, coverage and triggered-policy decompositions, the full monthly loss distribution, and contract-to-payment lineage; the superseded rows are retained only as synthetic calibration and provenance evidence, not as market observations.

The submitted historical, Normal, and EVT-GPD VaR/TVaR work is applied consistently to the same 1,000 monthly aggregate insurer-paid-loss observations, with explicit tail conventions, EVT threshold checks, and the retained-loss transformation X_R=min(X,d). The Delta-Gamma submission is preserved as a separate hypothetical frequency-severity teaching example, not as a fourth estimator of the entity-first portfolio loss; the submitted autoregressive route is not used because the synthetic month indices are not a chronological time series.

The raw notebook functions for utility, risk aversion, maximum premiums, and stop-loss insurance were rebuilt as validated finite-sample calculations over all 1,000 monthly paid-loss observations. The page compares exponential (CARA), logarithmic, and power utility at a common local absolute-risk-aversion level, enforces each wealth domain, solves the expected-utility premium exactly, splits X into retained and ceded layers, and compares the insurer's maximum price for the ceded layer with the reinsurer's net minimum E[X_C].

The student's submitted approximation file implements the Normal, Normal Power, and translated-gamma methods. The current page applies them to the first three moments of each selected policy's complete 1,000-month paid-loss distribution, including zero months and variable positive payments; the independent benchmark removes only cross-policy covariance and is compared with the same-month empirical aggregate that retains shared-accident dependence. The separately submitted convolution file combines two aggregate accident-count distributions, so it remains provenance evidence but is not presented as an individual-policy loss calculation. The fixed-benefit Bernoulli reduction is not used for portfolio results.

The Chapter 3 submissions were consolidated into a coverage-stratified compound-loss workflow: Poisson and negative-binomial claim-frequency fitting; Gamma, inverse-Gaussian, exponential-mixture, lognormal, and Pareto severity fitting with AIC comparison; Panjer, FFT, and reproducible Monte Carlo aggregate-distribution routes; moment and Normal-approximation checks; own-damage plus liability reconciliation; and an empirical stop-loss continuation. Invalid sparse-vector normalization and fragile hard-coded paths were not reused, and physical-accident frequency remains a diagnostic rather than a substitute for policy-claim frequency.

The submitted Chapter 4 heavy-tail, discrete-time ruin exercise is connected to the reconciled 1,000-month portfolio-loss sample and the shared monthly stop-loss definition S=min(X,d). The page uses seeded empirical resampling to estimate finite-horizon first ruin under c=(1+theta)E[S], reports Monte Carlo uncertainty and first-ruin timing, visualizes surplus paths, and tests sensitivity to initial capital. It deliberately reports neither an ultimate-ruin probability nor a Lundberg bound, because the source Pareto component does not justify a finite positive moment-generating function.
